newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore rubber up on buying by China, others.
newsitem.headline: Singapore rubber up on buying by China, others.

text.p: The Singapore rubber market closed slightly higher on Tuesday due to modest buying by Chinese and Indonesian buyers engaged in mild shortcovering in the market, dealers said.

"The Chinese bought some RSS3 rubber although it tapered off today and the Indonesians were also doing some hedging for TSR20 rubber. Some Japanese were also making inquiries in the market," a trader said.
"Most of the major consumers were not really in the market. I think some of them asked for price quotes, but they did not come in," another dealer said.
Dealers said the modest volumes in the Tokyo and Kobe rubber markets kept sentiment in the local trade subdued.
"The manufacturers here were mostly sidelined. Apparently, they feel prices will still soften further," a dealer said.
The market was looking at whether the International Natural Rubber Organisation (INRO) will intervene to prop up prices, but the prospect seems unlikely for now, traders said.
At around 0945 GMT, August RSS3 was seen at 89.50 U.S. cents a kg from 89.00 cents. September TSR20 was seen at 133.00 Singapore cents (93 U.S. cents) a kg from 131.00 cents.
